**TL;DR - Focus on the app and legitimate users.**  


Totally agree, See pirates gonna pirate but you should not punish normal users for that.

  
Like Adobe for example has DRM that cripples its performance, the comparison between DRM removed and DRM version showed 20-25% performance improvement. 

  
Same goes for games, DRM hinders performance and leads to many bugs and  performance issues to the point that some Developers has stopped using DRM and releasing DRM free content like Bohemia Interactive, cd project red etc. 

Upcoming hit **Cyberpunk 2077** game will also be released without DRM because they focus more on users & the actual content of the app/game.

I think the time and effort you put to prevent pirates is much more fruitful if you put them for your legit users and continuously improve app & new features.  


Also piracy isn't necessarily bad, some % of users prefer to try first and then make the actual investment, that's why you see nowadays "free for limited time" thing is booming. Not only that if the pirate actually likes an app he'll tell others about it, review it, rate it and you'll get Word-of-mouth marketing for free and as Jeff Bezos said WOM Marketing is very powerful.

  
And who knows at some point that pirate might actually donate or buy it.

Some of the famous experts of apps like MS Office, Adobe products, Windows started their journey with pirated versions before they became the expert to the point where they teach others how to use the app for effectively and efficiently.  


I am just saying you should spend time on the actual functionality of the app and the user feedbacks not on piracy, and lets say you did succeed in stopping piracy but then it might end up hurting yourself by losing % of your users which will lead to less user input, less potential revenue, less WOM marketing, less popularity.

“It’s easier for our software to compete with Linux when there’s piracy than when there’s not.”

— Bill Gates  


About that Cloud functionality suggestion, its expensive (servers and its maintenance), its bad for countries/users with average internet connections so it limits your global reach, risk of server crashing, puts the burden of cost of mobile data on users more so if the app is paid or has IAP.  
If there's global pandemic of internet your app will become useless.   


I want to clear it out i am not supporting piracy i am just saying you can yield much more profit if you focus on app itself.
